text_fidelity_a:
Pflueger President Spinning Reel, Fishing Reel, Right/Left Handle Position, Graphite Body and Rotor, Corrosion-Resistant, Aluminum Spool, Front Drag System I can't say enough about this reel. I don't have a lot of money, but I love to fish. One day I decided I was going to treat myself and buy a $150 reel. I spent any hour and a half in Cabela's and about the same at Sportsman's. I tried every reel in the place, and still ended up with the Pres 30. It's just the best feeling reel I've ever used, and I've borrowed plenty over my 40+ years.

But it's not just great to play with in the store. I've caught probably 200 trout on mine, and it's been beat up. Dropped, submerged, dragged through mud, and covered in clay. I treated it the same way I did my Abu ProMax, and that piece of garbage died after 2 months.

If you're looking for a great reel and you have $150 to spend, get this and use the extra money to buy a nice rod, some good copoly line, and gas up your truck. Go fish!

Sivan Pilates Ring, Black, 35cm I really wanted to like this. But, do you see those three awkward exercises on the cover picture? Those are really the only three things you can do with this. #1: Squeeze your legs together, #2: Squeeze your arms together to work on your triceps, and #3, squeeze your ankles together. The big problem that I have with this is that those three exercises are only for extremely tiny muscle groups. That means that you have much more chance of getting injured than you do of this having a good place in a full-body workout.

I got it because I thought it would work for a lot more exercises. But, you can't push it against the ground or any other surface. It will spring up and slip away. You can't pull on it. You can only push on it. So, you need two appendages to carefully push it together. So that leaves only pushing it together with your arms or pushing it together with your legs. You know those machines at the gym that nobody uses? This lets you do those exercises at home with just a hoop.

The nice aspects are that it's high quality, and the resistance isn't too intense, so anyone could use it. But, you really should get some better equipment than this.
text_fidelity_b: Sivan Pilates Ring, Black, 35cm

text_fidelity_a: Wenzel Blue Jay 25 Degree Sleeping Bag I love these bags! Got two of them to zip together for a queen sized air mattress. First off, they are big and roomy. But nicely, they don't get too warm either. The zipper can be opened from either end, and has a velcro flap at the top to keep it from coming unzipped during the night. Zippers work great and two zip together perfectly. The only reason they didn't get 5 stars is due to the elastic bands to hold it rolled up and the stuff sack. The elastic bands are sewn to the bag and I've had them before on other bags. After a couple of years, they lose their elasticity and are useless. Attached compression straps would be much better. The stuff sack is a little bit too lightweight to last very long and the seams are not reinforced, so it won't be long before it becomes torn up. I'm going to double stitch the seams to hopefully help is last a little longer. Overall, a great comfortable roomy sleeping bag that should hold up well despite a somewhat cheap stuff sack.

Bike Handlebar Mirror 2 Pack - Rotatable And Adjustable Wide Angle Rear View Shockproof Convex Mirror Universal For Bike Bicycle I like these mirrors, I typically ride against traffic, as it's easier to keep a lookout for drivers. The thing is, when someone is coming, I have to look over and see what the other lane is doing. That isn't always comfy, and I sometimes don't feel safe having to look over my shoulder. That's why I don't ride with traffic, because it's too often I have to look over myself to see what's behind me.

These mirrors help for both types of riding, but the problem is that even with them, it's hard to really see them until they're really close on you. It's better to have them than not, but it requires focusing on the mirrors to see a car from a fair bit away. I like the look of them, and the mounting isn't too bad, it has rubber pieces you can put into it to clamp down with, and once you do that, they're pretty stable. You do have really good visibility, and even if I can't see the cars from far away, it's a really pretty sight being able to see the world passing by you behind you. I like these, but I took a star off just because I wished I could see the cars better. Maybe if they were magnified they'd work better. Do get them, but if needing quick visibility on the cars behind you is very important, skip these, look for magnified mirrors more similar to car mirrors.

I used it on our Eucalyptus patio table, chairs and side tables. After washing and scrubbing each piece, then sanding with 150 grit then 220 grit and wiping down with a tack cloth, I put on two thin coats. I used a microfiber 12" x 12" cloth to apply it. I waited 8 hours between coats. The furniture came out with a rich, deep golden color. Extremely happy with the results.

I purchased a quart. It was enough for a 6 foot patio dining table, 6 patio dining chairs and 3 side tables with a little bit left.

The key is to use thin coats and wait at least 8 hours between coats. I also used a dry microfiber cloth to wipe off any excess about 15 minutes after applying.

text_fidelity_a: H2OSUP Sit-On-Top Kayak Seat,Inflatable Paddle Board Universal/Adjustable/Detachable/Soft Padded Boat Seat and Backrest with Storage Bag for Fishing/Kayaking/ Rafting / Canoeing My wife and I recently got a H2OSUP and while my wife loves the SUP aspect, I have ankles that spent years of athletics and to that end, as I age, they don’t like standing on an SUP as much or as long. I saw this H2OSUP Sit-On-Top Kayak Seat and grabbed it! I spend most of my time on SUPs seated in order to keep from growing pain. I am thrilled I grabbed it! Unfortunately, we haven’t been able to get on the water as we’d hoped. Now with winter bearing down... but we have tested out the SUPs and tried this H2OSUP Sit-On-Top Kayak Seat on top - the H20 SUP products all seem to be - to our beginner knowledge - an excellent product line. So when I saw it was an H20 seat, I expected the same - I was right. The seat is well constructed of good materials, everything stitched and assembled well. Not having done this before (our tour SUPs never had seats) it was easy to fugue out how to put it together - attach - with common sense. Attach the clips to the 4 D Rings on the surface, and you’re ready to go. The seat is comfortable, holds well in place, and seems like it’ll give decent support. This is not a seat in that you can recline or that it’ll give you the same support as a chair. But with the attached straps that hold it in place, able to be adjusted for tension, you get a pretty decent amount of support while seated. I’m carrying a bit of extra weight, yet once seated and leaning back, I felt comfortable and like if I were on water, it would help me maintain comfort and help in supporting my back. In other words, I think it’ll work fine on the water. The seat is comfortable. I was wearing shorts, but I felt like I would be able to sit for a decent length of time and find it comfortable - not to mention be okay if I and the seat were wet. We are most likely to use these SUPs on salt water, so we plan to rinse them all off extensively with fresh water post-use in order to keep and maintain the integrity and longevity of the seat, SUP, and other supplies. In the end, my wife and I both feel like this H2OSUP Sit-On-Top Kayak Seat will turn our SUP into a great SUP-Kayak combination, and allow us more than one use and way to enjoy them. The H20 product line again seems like it’s quality and something we would consider getting again.

text_fidelity_a: Grizzly Fitness Reversible Knee Sleeve I have knee arthritis in both knees, though one much more noticeably than the other, and have had a torn meniscus in said same knee.  I had arthroscopic surgery for the tear, which helped, but I never quite got over the surgery.  And, my arthritis is still very apparent.  I have used elastic cloth knee braces for the most part but got a wild hair and decided to try a neoprene knee brace.  I've tried Mueller's, Grizzly's, and TK's.  With Mueller's, it just didn't feel right.  The small TK was TOO small; the Medium was gappy.  You know what I mean.  The Grizzly Medium was just right.  When I first got it, I thought, there's no way I'm getting that tiny thing over my giant deformed knee.  But, with not that much effort I DID.  And, it wasn't gappy.  And, I was doing step aerobics (low impact) comfortably - which I haven't in ages.  I was and am thrilled.  For me, this thing is a game changer.  I think that part of my problem is that my knee innards are actually sloshing around in there.  It FEELS like that, but with this support, no sloshing.  My knee is stablized.  My knee is one bendable thing instead of a bunch of loose parts.  My knee is happy.  I am happy.  I'm MORE than happy.  Like I said.  I'm thrilled.

text_fidelity_a:
OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12" This is my first use of a trap -- used for cats in NE suburban backyard. Pretty good product: caught 5 cats, 2 possums and 1 raccoon in a couple of months over this winter. There were 3 escapees.
Some suggestions:
The trap I received was an entirely wire grid device. Older photos show a solid sheet metal closing door.
Several of the clips from critical places had not been installed and were rattling about in the box. In particular, one of two clips that holds the
trap door to the roof of the trap had to be installed or substituted for with wire. These clips are not the sturdiest. One escapee pulled one loose.
I found that it took some practice to set the trap to have a just so sensitivity, and a little bending of the spring catch. It's not complicated, but plan on practicing. Furthermore, desperate animals will dig up enough soil to cover many important joints, so there is need for cleaning and oiling to keep the mechanism working properly. Snow or soil underneath the trap lever will prevent closure.
I also found that the rear door closure with a large clip and a metal rod is not adequate. A small, determined animal can escape. I simply added a piece of telephone wire to hold the rear door to the roof of the trap securely.
text_fidelity_b: OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12"

It took a little playing around with the wraps to get the right amount of tension, but once I figured that out I found the wrist support to be excellent. My grip isn't unusually strong, and I've not had that happen with other good quality gloves. Most of my work with these gloves included kettlebells, dumbbells, and medicine balls, so I don't think it was the gear either.

Although I ended up returning these gloves, I think they could be right for other people. And I can't fault customer service since they accepted my return with no question. The time between receipt of the product and the return deadline is more than ample to try these out for yourself. If you're on the fence, I'd say it's worth giving these a go. Grizzly Gear Emergency Survival Mylar Thermal 2 Person Sleeping Bag - Accommodates 2 Adults - 64" X 87" As you know, the point of these emergency blankets is to use them when everything else has failed. You are not at home (or the power and gas is out), you can't get to relatives, a hotel, or a Red Cross shelter... Or perhaps you are literally lost in the woods and thanking your lucky stars you threw an emergency blanket in your daypack..

The only difference here is that two people can fit, and if you have ever had to worry about hyperthermia, you know that the body heat of another is about the only way to bring up the body heat of the severely chilled person.

On a trail crew as an older teen and we got one guy into a fairly serious hyperthermia situation after using a cold mountain lake to float materials for trail bridges a shorter distance than hiking them around the lake. Great idea, but several us of took too many trips. We had a sleeping bag with us in a day kit, but it lost most of its thermal capacity when it got wet from the guys soaked clothes (dumb us: take the wet clothes off first!...) One of these emergency blankets and with room for a second person would have been an easier way to get him back to normal, and taken a lot less space.

From a price point of view, you can find single blankets for $5 to $20 bucks, depending on sale prices, quality and so forth. Thus, this double-sized version is priced at essentially no difference in cost and works for two. Construction is great. Four stars only because it's not a super premium version (which of course would cost more.) (EDITED to five stars, responding to a comment -- I agree.) These are designed for emergencies, so you are not buying this for multiple uses. This version seems to be at the right price point.

Hope this is helpful.

text_fidelity_a:
Bike Hoist Bicycle Lift for Garage Ceiling Storage, Heavy Duty Mountain Bicycle Hanging Rack with 3 Pulley and 45 ft Adjustable Rope | 100 lb Capacity You could assemble the components for a better bike hoisting system at any decent hardware store, but the part you would buy would cost two or three times as much, and you would spend a fair amount of time figuring out what to buy and how to assemble it.

I see several review that report the packaging indicates a lesser weight capacity than the 100 lb indicated in the listing. My packaging shows the weight capacity as 45 kg -- 100 lb. Regardless, I am confident that, in fact, much more than 100 lb. could be supported by this hardware. The actual limiting factor on weight capacity will not be the hardware provided, but rather the installation method. The box includes screws with plastic anchors that are normally used for installing screws in sheetrock. Anyone who uses those to attach to a sheetrock ceiling will almost certainly have a problem. Even if the plastic anchors are used to attach the hardware to wood trusses the result will be weaker than if screwed directly into the wood after a proper size hole has been pre-drilled. Other reviews contain suggestions for mounting. The instructions provided fail to provide guidance on the need for a secure mounting.

It is easy to overlook on the installation instructions the correct routing of the rope used for lifting. There is a hole in the cam lock fitting through which the cord should be threaded. Unfortunately the hole is barely large enough for the provided rope, which would make it difficult to upsize the rope.

Which brings me to the issue of the gaps between pulley cheeks and the sheaves. The gap is enough that the provided rope can jump out of the sheave groove and become wedged. The sheaves are designed so that squeezing the cheeks to reduce the gap results in friction at the axle before the gap is significantly reduced. While a larger rope could eliminate the risk of jamming, the hole in the cam lock does not permit such a substitution. It is for this reason, and the potential that a person could be misled by the plastic sheetrock anchors and fail to attach to solid wood, that I am giving 4 stars rather than 5.

Additional comments -- As others mention, the hooks to hang the bike do not really have enough curve to hold securely and you probably will need to do some bending to get a good result. My seat does not have a structure to which the hooks would attach, so I use a cord under a frame section and secure the hooks to that. If you have a speedometer or the like mounted on handle bars there is a possibility of conflict with hooks, and you may need to be careful to avoid damage to any wire connecting to a sensor. The cleat provided to tie off the rope when the bike is lifted is definitely pretty cheesy, but the cam lock is good enough that the cleat is really not needed. If you are a belt and suspenders person you might want to upgrade the cleat. Otherwise the cleat basically just provides a method to get excess rope out of the way.

So while this is not perfect, it provides a good solution at a good price, and I would buy another one if I had a second bike.

text_fidelity_a:
POLAR FT60 Heart Rate Monitor Round TWO! I'd bought this identical HRM kit back in February 2014. From day one, I'd get WILDLY erratic readings on the heart rate - but that's ok, cuz I am actually from Planet Mars. No machine in any gym, nor any kind of heart rate monitor on Planet Earth works consistently on me. I either get zero reading (when my Martian paws are on the piece of exercise equipment) or I get rates that jump from 189 to 60 to 132, and so on. Don't tell the NSA, because I'm here on a secret mission: to see if my second purchase of this Polar FT60 HRM works. I should've registered my initial purchase back in Feb, but being a foolish optimist, I used the HRM daily - till it plain died on me long about August. I stopped getting any kind of reading between the transmitter and the device - even after new batteries were inserted. So I assumed it was a goner.

What I LOVE about this HRM:
- It gives me the data I need to stick with my fitness program: how many minutes spent in zone 1, 2, & 3 (based on initial VO2 reading and the 6-min fitness test I took first time I took it to the gym); my total calories burned and what percentage of them were fat; my average and max heart rate (which, on the first device I purchased gave the "accurately" bizarre ranges of 189 to 62, but I know why that is). That is ALL I need to know. I'm not a marathon runner or even daily runner. My goal is to burn 400+ calories in a variety of ways at the gym (or outdoors) on most days of the week. I don't need to know my footfall, cadence, how much foot is on the ground every nano-second, my GPS coordinate, or about 100 other functions that other HRMs provide (and which are no doubt of interest to the athlete wearing them).
- It's easy to find your VO2 (well, maybe it's based on a lame algorithm, but I have SOME number to work with)
- It's compatible with ALL the machines in my gym, so I don't have to keep looking down at my wrist every few seconds (like I did with the Garmin) to see what my heart rate is - a BIG plus!
- It's pretty intuitive to operate, once you spend 5 min learning the main buttons.
- It's a good-looking watch
- It doesn't drain the battery like some of the Garmin devices (unless you shut off GPS and turn the device off)

What I HATE about the device (Product Development: READ ME FIRST)
- the buttons are CRIPPLINGLY PAINFUL to press. It's ridiculous, but no kidding, I had to press the dang buttons against a flat, hard piece of granite counter to actually get them to depress.
- OUCH! OUCH! OUCH! OUCH! OUCH! I have short nails, but they'd just slip off the button if I used them, so I use the fleshy tip of my now CRIPPLED, broken finger to press the idiotically STIFF buttons on this watch. I mean come ON: spend a nickel more and get some decent springs under these buttons, so I don't get arthritis from pressing them every day.
- These painful buttons drove me to THROW the whole kit away when it stopped working (my duh) and go buy a Garmin HRM right here at Amazon.com. Unfortunately, that device seems to require a PhD in Rocket Science to call up the right screens to find the few bits of data I was interested in. PLUS that device also gave very erratic readings, given that it was not made for a Martian, but rather an Earthling.
- I think that for the money paid, the Polar FT60 should *in theory* last longer than a scant 6 mos? The warranty is for 2 years, but I've read elsewhere (mostly from a few years back) that other folks complained about their device conking out.

I'm going to register this HRM and take good care of it, cuz despite the NUMBINGLY PAINFUL buttons, it is the only device that gives me the exact data I want to see after each workout.

Please Polar: Make these buttons easier to press, huh?
text_fidelity_b: POLAR FT60 Heart Rate Monitor

text_fidelity_a: Water Bottle with Fruit Infuser and Carrying Handle 27 Ounce NO BPA (Yellow) This water bottle has some definite pros and cons. Lets start with the good: for sure it's great to be able to drink fruit infused water! I don't drink any sodas or sugary drinks, so this is a great idea. The bottle is also very pretty (i got the yellow) and it's really awesome to see my yellow top with my yellow lemon slices in the bottle. It's also nice that the fruit is contained in the inner tube and not able to come out when poured. There is also a nice flip top with a handle so it can be clipped onto a bag or just carried by the little top handle. Thats about all the good points. The unfortunate problem with this bottle is that it doesn't allow you to drink all the water in the bottle! Because of where the holes are to let water in, it prevents you from finishing your last 2 inches of water. So thats a problem because if i want to finish my water i have to take the whole top off and then the wet tube with the fruit drips everywhere and it's just awkward. You also cant fill the bottle with water all the way up because the tube of fruit displaces so much of the water. Then on top of it, when you have drank about half of the bottle, the water isn't even touching the fruit anymore! Plus, when you go to drink it, it's hard to get any water out because the fruit from the tube bumps up against the water hole and blocks it. The water will come out but only a little bit, it's very obstructed. Then we have the problem of the flip top itself. It does seal well, however in order to open the top to drink it, you have to pinch your finger under this brittle plastic piece to open it. I feel like it's very difficult to open and hurts my finger. I also feel like it's so brittle its only a matter of time before it breaks. So, overall I don't see myself continuing to use this bottle. It doesn't hold much water and doesn't function very well. I did receive this product at a discount in exchange for a review and I always give my honest opinion.
text_fidelity_b: Water Bottle with Fruit Infuser and Carrying Handle 27 Ounce NO BPA (Yellow)

text_fidelity_a:
Incline Fit Resistance Bands (11pcs) - 5 Stackable Exercise Bands Ranging from 2 to 30 lbs of Resistance; Includes Zip-up Bag, Foam Handles, Ankle Strap, Door Anchor & Workout Book This set seems like a good, basic exercise-bands kit. There are 5 resistance bands:

yellow = extra light = 2-4 lbs resistance
blue = light = 4-6 lbs resistance
green = medium = 10-12 lbs resistance
black = heavy = 15-20 lbs resistance
red = extra heavy = 25-30 lbs resistance

You choose a band with the desired resistance, clip it to the 2 handles or a handle and the Velcro ankle strap, and do the desired exercises. There's also a "door anchor" nylon strap with a fat weight in one end. You thread the exercise band through the loop on one end on the anchor, then place it along the edge of the door and close the door. The fat end prevents the strap from slipping through the gape in the door and thus you can do some exercises with the exercise band centered above or level with you. This does, however, put some stress on the door. Not so much with the lighter weights, but I suspect it would with the heavier weights. The equipment seems well-made and so far I've had no problems with it in its first week of light use. They have a book with 18 exercises described and several illustrated with a color photo. They provide a lifetime warranty.

Some of their warnings:
-Do not overstretch the resistance bands [though they don't say exactly how far is too far]
-Always wear safety glasses when using resistance bands [and safety glasses are not included]
text_fidelity_b: Incline Fit Resistance Bands (11pcs) - 5 Stackable Exercise Bands Ranging from 2 to 30 lbs of Resistance; Includes Zip-up Bag, Foam Handles, Ankle Strap, Door Anchor & Workout Book

ABSOAR Cycling Bike Lights Front and Rear Silicone LED Water Resistant Headlights Tail Light High Intensity for Safety, 2 Pack Most headlights have a lens that casts forward, to amplify the LED(s) so that you can brightly see what is in front of you. This lens arrangement offers little-to-no side exposure to alert side drivers of your presence.

These lights are visible from the front or back (depending on your placement) PLUS from the sides.

I bicycle with four lights, solid and strobing white lights in the front and solid and strobing red lights in the back. Each of the front and back light has side strobe exposure.

I also wear a neon yellow reflective vest and drivers still turn right into me. I know to brake hard at a moment's notice and that knowledge has probably saved me an injury at least a few times.

After I brake hard and raise my hands in the air to say "WTF," the driver says, "I DIDN'T SEE YOU." Me, with all this regalia of lights and reflective strips on my vest, "Seriously?"

Drivers just don't think. They just turn the wheel and apply pressure to the foot controls.

Just do the best you can and make certain that you have side light coverage.
text_fidelity_b: ABSOAR Cycling Bike Lights Front and Rear Silicone LED Water Resistant Headlights Tail Light High Intensity for Safety, 2 Pack

Exped Air Pillow, Medium I bought three of these bad boys mostly based on a whim to have a pillow and the thoughts of comfort when sleeping. I've recently equipped my family to be able to do some decent backpacking. These were sort of afterthoughts.

I based my choices largely on Amazon user reviews. With few exceptions, and I hope we shan't be one, I was taken with the price, size and comfort.

I'm looking forward to giving this a night's use.

EDIT 08-25-2013
After a week of backpacking use, this little pillow became my best friend. As it is I already have problems with my neck and shoulder. Throw in an extra 40+ lbs tucked into my [[ASIN:B004R7L7YU ALPS OutdoorZ Commander Freighter Frame Plus Pack Bag, 5250 Cubic Inches]] including sleeping bag, tent, ground pad, clothing, food... you know, essentials, and I was a tired, sore puppy each night.

This pillow was exactly what I wanted and needed. It was comfortable when inflated, cushioned the head nicely whether laying on my side or back and took up minimal space and weight when deflated. I HIGHLY recommend this.

I hope it continues to give me nights upon nights of comfort and rest. I'd hate to think of it failing me when I needed it most.

Sunya 300 Win MAG Boresighter with Carrying Bag, 7.62x67 Red Laser Bore Sight Includes 2 Sets Battery Yes, this SUNYA Laser Bore Sight is specifically designed for rifles in 7.62X39 caliber. With ammo currently costing what it does (avg 50 cents per round of 7.62X39) the purchase of this handy boresighter can save you a lot of money -- especially if you need it for more than one rifle. Or perhaps lend it to a friend and build up a few brownie points.

Simply twist off the end cap, insert 3 batteries, and twist the cap back on. The laser should light up. Make sure that your rifle is unloaded and the charging handle is in the back position. Insert the boresighter and line up the laser to your of point of aim. Do not pull the trigger or release the charging handle. Either can cause damage to your boresighter.

Then mount your scope (red dot, holographic sight) and adjust the point of aim to the laser. Now you have a good frame of reference for when you go to fine-tune your sights at the range. Easy to use, saves on ammo costs, and allows you as much time as you need at home to line up your sights without having "range pressure".

You can purchase boresighters for virtually any caliber of rifle/pistol. Just remember that you're going to zero your firearm at a certain distance and with specific ammo. Changing the distance or trying different brands of ammo will result in differing results. However it is easy to repeat the steps to help zero any change in ammunition.
text_fidelity_b: Sunya 300 Win MAG Boresighter with Carrying Bag, 7.62x67 Red Laser Bore Sight Includes 2 Sets Battery

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Little Jumpers Trampoline 786 I do not recommend the Alex Little Jumper Trampoline unless space is an issue. For $23 less you can purchase the significantly larger and more stable [[ASIN:B008BIV87M Bazoongi 48" Trampoline Bouncer with Easy Hold Handle Bar - Sunshine Yellow. Special Exclusive Limited Edition]].

The instructions are worthless. For example, one part states to "attach the bungee cord to the cord lock by pulling the knotted end of the cord tight". Can I just start by saying "What?" Well there is no knotted end, so you have to create it, though it doesn't really tell you how to do that. Then you have the issue of only three helpful images for the entire manual. And I probably need to start by saying I like to consider myself rather capable when it comes to assembling items and frames of structures having helped my father build our homes and additions. The instructions also do not elaborate where the knotted end should go in reference to the trampoline itself. You can figure out where it needs to go in the medal cord lock, but not on the trampoline itself. The only picture shows half of the trampoline having the cord wrapped around it so you are left wondering what the starting point looks like.

I hazarded a guess and just went with it at that point. Once I wrapped everything around and made sure that I pulled the cord tight several times I then tied it off. The instructions are then once again really vague; therefore I knotted the last end of the cord by itself and pulled it through the medal fastener. I then proceeded to knot the last end of the cord that I had just wrapped around with the beginning part of the cord to ensure an additional sense of security. The instructions mention nothing of this but after looking at the final results, with pieces of cord jutting out in random places, I knew that my three youngest would see that as an invitation to mess with it. So I knotted both ends together, and I did that twice. My kids can be rather problematic.

The directions then tell you to place the cover on the trampoline, making sure that it fits. Once again, the instructions lack on details. They do not specify that the cover should be placed in a specific direction. I used the writing on the cover as an indication for direction, placing the writing outwards where the handle will go. Otherwise, the cover does not fit. I found this out through trial and error, of course. There are also plastic clips that apparently must be clipped to the trampoline in some fashion, that you obviously have to figure out on your own. The most obvious thing was to clip them to the bungee cords that were wrapped around the trampoline.

The next step is to secure the handle. And yet again, those wonderful directions prove that they are pointless. I finally just put the small yellow bar into the curved handle portion (not attaching to the trampoline base yet) to get a sense of where it should go in the actual trampoline frame. I was then able to figure out which direction it faced, knowing that screws would be added at the end. REALLY not clear, but I was able to figure out having put together dozens of pieces before.

All in all, given that it was purchased at a discounted price, it will work out fine in addition to our other in home trampoline. This might be alright for one child, but it would definitely not work for my three kids (4 yr old twins and a 2 yr old) if I did not have the second larger trampoline. They are the ultimate test in terms of durability for any toy and this one is unfortunately not built for heavy duty usage. This might be fine on its own for occasional use from a calmer child, which none of mine are.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Little Jumpers Trampoline 786

SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black There is a major difference between this tube and its non thorn-resistant counterparts. The difference translates to a 3x larger package and a 3x stiffer inner tube. Whether this means that it will intercede on your behalf when penetrating objects attempt to derail your day, time will tell. But I can tell you that:

1) It takes some effort to stuff this piece of salami into your tire. It doesn't bend willingly.
2) It takes some getting used to on the road. Your tire will absorb less shock from road imperfections, resulting in a harsh ride. It's not like riding on solid rubber, but it's not as soft as a regular inner tube.

In my opinion, the harsh ride is worth it on a daily commuter, where reliability is paramount. I'm not sure if I'd use this on a recreational bike. A suspension bike may be fine.

Update: after a week or two, I stopped noticing the stiffer ride quality. Also, I have about 50lbs extra on that rear wheel, so my experience may not be typical (it's an e-bike).

text_fidelity_a: Reebok Adjustable Weighted Belt I used the belt for the first time today, after the particular weight vest I bought turned out to be a total loss (and cost me $12 to return to Amazon, thank you very much).  This belt was an improvement, but that's not saying much. To begin with, the strap that attaches to one end of the weighted tube appears to have been sewn or attached vertically, rather than horizontally.  This means that when you attach the belt to its fastener on the other side (which is attached properly-i.e. horizontally), the strap is twisted. So there is minor discomfort even before you've done any exercise. The belt does cinch nicely, and shifts just slightly side-to-side during (my relatively mild) walking exercizes- however, I did not try any moves that involved jumping up and down, specifically because I was afraid that the weight would bounce up and down and be very uncomfortable .  The darn thing is just bulky- about as big around as a water bottle, and rests right along the hips. All the weight is in the back, which throws off your stride- also, you can't move your arms very freely,and you have to make a pretty conscious effort to keep your swinging elbows from whacking the thing each time you stride. text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included) The fitbit as it comes out of the box (in late 2020) has lots of bugs. The settings function will lock it up if you try to use it. The weather app errors. It will not sync reliably. You would be thinking about returning it right now. But if you do some internet searches, you will find that these are known bugs that it leaves the factory with. If you install the mobile app, sync it and wait about 2 - 3 days the nyou will get the update that makes things work as they should. Do NOT uninstall the weather function of the fitbit just because it won't sync. If you do, it will no longer be available to re-install when device is updated. Just leave it there and wait for the update. Then weather and settings will work and syncing will become reliable.

It's absurd that fitbit would release such a defective product, but they do and they don't make any effort to tell you about the needed update.

After updating, it is quite a handy little tracker. The only fitbit tracker with a built in gps so you don't need to take your phone along. However be warned that your battery if fully charges will only last 4 - 5 hours when using the gps. It also takes a lot of time away from the standby time remaining.

Another feature they don't try to explain properly is the Spotify integration. Your fitbit can act as a very basic remote control for Spotify, but only if you subscribe to Spotify Premium. This means that to use the Spotify remote control feature you need 1) a paid Spotify subscription and 2) you need to have your phone with you. No music can be downloaded to the fitbit. It is just a simple play/stop/skip remote function for your phone and Spotify paid.

So those are all the things that fitbit doesn't want to tell you even after you buy it. After you get it updated, it is essentially a Charge 3 with built in battery sucking gps and paid Spotify remote control.

If you are new to fitbit and don't mind all the hassles getting it working right, it is a great little tracker. If you are thinking about upgrading from a fitbit Charge 3, the built in gps and Spotify remotes are the main differences.

Update: After all this it would never sync reliably. I would always have to reboot the device twice in a row to get sync started again. This hat do be done about every 36 hours.

Returned. Not worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included)

We're all heading into the basement where we have collected fun games over the years, like an air hockey table, Foosball, electronic darts, an electronic basketball hoop....and now our new addition, the light-up lawn darts game. It is a blast in the basement (although we keep a little bit of lighting on). This is so much fun, and really adds a unique game to break up our wintertime boredom.

Here are a few tips that may help you.

1) We put a few streaks of glow-in-the-dark paint on the rings, to brighten them up a bit, and it worked wonderfully. We got this super bright green glow in the dark paint for about $10 here on Amazon and it worked great: [[ASIN:B00BD63C8W Ultra Green V10 Glow in the Dark Paint 1/2Oz]]

2) Don't give a second thought to replacing the batteries. It's easy. I buy all my replacement button batteries from Amazon. In fact, these lawn darts take the LR41 batteries, which you can get 10 of them from Amazon for about $6: [[ASIN:B000AQ7ME6 Maxell Watch Battery Button Cell LR41 AG3 192 Pack of 10 Batteries]]. Or if you want more, you can get 50 of them for about $13-14: [[ASIN:B0057ON2JA 50 Pack Maxell LR41 AG3 192 button cell battery "NEW HOLOGRAM PACKAGE "]] .

3) If you need replacement parts, which is honestly unlikely, as these things are sturdy as heck. And if you need information on replacement parts, you can email: replacementparts@franklinsports.com or you can call 1-781-341-5178.

Thanks for reading my review. I sure hope it helped you.

text_fidelity_a: FitDesk Desk Bike 3.0 - Folding Exercise Bike for Work from Home Fitness, Stationary Bike and Desk Exercise Equipment with Built-in Tablet Holder, Bike Desk Workout Equipment, Fully Adjustable & Lightweight So far so good.  I will say this is an initial review so I will mostly cover set-up and first impressions since I've only ridden the bike once so far.  Will do a follow up review later to better rate how it holds up.  Other reviewers have said two hours to assemble, and I found this to be extremely accurate for one person.  If the bike will go up or down stairs, recommend opening the box near the door and taking the individual pieces one at a time.  The design was smart for an assemble yourself device, as they put most of the mounting bolts in the places they go to make things easier.  All the tools you need are included in the box, but I highly recommend bringing your own socket wrench with a 13mm socket for the seat mounts at minimum.  This will make things a whole lot easier for you.  I used the included tools for everything else which worked fine.  I did use the seat extender because I'm 5'11", but it was a tough call for me since my wife is 5'8" and it is recommended for folks that are 5'9" and taller.  But with my socket wrench it will be easy to remove if she can't reach the pedals.  The seat is not particularly easy to adjust up and down, but I sprayed a little WD-40 on the metal and it made it slightly better.  It's sturdy once you have it at the level you want it.  The seat back folds forward, and has a lock bolt to prevent it from moving backwards, or to adjust to your level of comfort.  I took out the lock bold and used one of the extra adjustment knobs which fits in that hole too and seems more natural to use, and I put the nut from the lock bolt on it to secure it.  Not in the instructions, but it works better for me that way.  The massage bar is useful to me for added stability too.  You can hold onto that instead of the desk, or use it for added stability for your forearms when using your laptop or tablet.  I threaded the securing band through the top upper hole and only use that for a laptop since I have a pillow style holder that sits nicely on the desk for my tablet.  Typing is pretty seamless on the lower resistance levels, although I expect to be watching Netflix movies most of the time so I have a better handle on my riding time without paying any more attention to it than length of whatever show I choose to zone out to.  I did connect the meter and it seems to work fine, but so far I don't pay any attention to the calorie counter or other readings.  I had thought about ordering a rubber mat to go under it because of our squeaky hardwood floors, but the seats on the bottom sit quietly and the machine doesn't make much noise.  I would recommend having a towel handy though as this does offer a real cardio workout and you will perspire unlike the guy in the picture Amazon has here.  My last comment relates to the value.  I pondered over the $6499 Expresso bike available here on Amazon long and hard because it seems to be the latest in VR bicycle technology before choosing this machine.  The high tech gadget lover in me drooled over that at first glance.  In the end analysis I just couldn't justify paying that kind of money and then possibly finding out I couldn't dedicate the required willpower to get on it regularly.  For less than 5% of that cost I really think I will use this one, and won't have to worry about signing up for an expensive membership once the free trial expires on that other choice.  This machine makes a whole lot more sense to me in the long run.  I absolutely think it is worth the cost- so far.  Once I get into better shape with it, I'll add more to this review- and hope this is helpful to you for now.
text_fidelity_b: FitDesk Desk Bike 3.0 - Folding Exercise Bike for Work from Home Fitness, Stationary Bike and Desk Exercise Equipment with Built-in Tablet Holder, Bike Desk Workout Equipment, Fully Adjustable & Lightweight

NHL Sting Ray Air Powered Hockey Table - 84 Inch - Features Scratch Resistant Material, Automatic Scoring, and Complete with All Accessories Mostly this is excellent, but it could have been so much more!

Putting this together is easy enough, nicer to have two pairs of hands on the job, no problem with only one. Then you get to use it. Lets start with whats right.
You plug it in, pop up the score board, switch it all on and you are off! The sound effects really help, the fun is fast and furious, the game play is great. It senses goals well, had no false goals or missed ones - just perfect.

What really lets this down is the power. The line to an outlet has a little inline rotating switch (like you get on cheap light fittings) just hanging below the table so you have to scramble on the floor to start and stop the fan.
The gaming computer runs on batteries! The batteries go to a plug on the computer! How stupid is that?
There should be a toggle switch on the underside of the table. That should power the fan, AND a 3.5 v power pack for the computer. For the price, it is insane that it does not have this, and I would see that as a deal breaker. I dont want to have to get on my back, underneath the table, unscrewing the battery case and replacing the batteries once every few months. I am modifying mine to work of one simple switch. That is how it should have shipped.

Marcy 3-Tier Dumbbell Rack Multilevel Weight Storage Organizer for Home Gym DBR-86 Tired of storing your dumbbells in corners or under the bed? I was and I chose this Apex rack because I like the slight slant, like we have in our fitness room and it looked sturdy in the photos. It IS sturdy up to the listed weight capacity and it is stable on the floor. Some assembly is required. The 'parts' come nicely wrapped and shrink wrapped nuts, bolts and washers kept the project in order while I was putting things together. My unit came with holes matching up nicely: it is always a good idea to leave the fasteners a little loose until the pieces are all fitted together, since some nudging is almost always required at some point to achieve a proper alignment. Be sure to tighten things then. I do NOT have a matching set of hand weights so I was interesting to see how well/IF the shorter, lighter weights would fit on the rack as I hoped. My SHORTEST weight is a 4 LB 'Yes4All' coated vinyl number, 6 3/4-inches end-to-end and it just fits securely on the rack. Shorter length weights would fall through the front and back rails any way you can install the rails.

I keep my weights and rack in a large walk-in closet where the rack fits under the clothes bars. I only have a few weights here but I have found that the bottom rails work fine as a shoe rack. Now both the weights and the shoes are being kept in good order.

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Sirrus 24 Women's Hiking Backpack I have an Osprey Sirrus 36 backpack that I bought at a local retailer a few years ago. I got this Sirrus 24 hoping the smaller version will be great for shorter day hikes that we often go on. it is good, but I'm having trouble getting it to fit me well.

What's good: This pack overall has an excellent amount of space for day hikes. the waist pockets are plenty roomy to hold things you need at your finger tips - keys, lip balm, small snacks (Gu, powerbar, etc). There is an internal pocket to hold a water bladder and a hole for the straw. It does NOT come with a water bladder. I use the bladder and straw tube that came with my other Osprey Sirrus 36 pack and that works great. The side pockets are deep, much deeper than on the other pack so they hold my hiking hat easily without worry of it falling out.

What's not so good: Really the only problem I have with this pack, as mentioned previously, is trying to get the right fit. I was thrilled with all the adjustments you can make to this pack to get it properly fitted, but so far I have not found that "sweet spot" where it fits comfortably. I've worn it on 4 hikes so far - from 7 to 14 mile day hikes on mountainous terrain. It has been good, just not as great a fit as the Sirrus 36. It could be that I'm just used to the way my old pack fits so I'll keep using this one intermittently to get used to it.

The fit: the back straps have a really neat feature where you can adjust the straps for a longer or shorter torso - I am only 5'2" tall and am short-waisted. So I've tried it on the shortest and places in between but it still hasn't felt perfect. I may just need to go into a local outfitter and have it professional fit to me so that I will have the correct fit.

bottom line - this is a really nice backpack. It is definitely high quality and holds plenty of stuff for long day hikes.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Sirrus 24 Women's Hiking Backpack

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump Grabbed one of these on sale on Black Friday, and finally got to try it out. Goes together easily and not difficult to pump up. One person can carry it, though it's less awkward for two. Between the netting on the front and the stowage in the stern behind the seat, we were able to take all our stuff with us and not have to worry about possible pilferage.

The instructions are a bit vague, so take note that there are TWO chambers to inflate, and the first one to be inflated is NOT the obvious top chamber (with the number 2 beside it), but the hidden number 1 chamber, which is located on the starboard (right) side, inside wall above the floor and a little aft of the middle of the boat. Each valve has two lids, one on top of the other; undo the upper one (with the 4-lobed lid) to inflate, and undo the lower lid (larger and round) to deflate. Don't over tighten the upper lid, or it's difficult to open it without the bottom lid opening too, and losing air. You may hear a hissing sound while inflating the second chamber, but don't worry—the air passage narrows at one point and it tends to hiss while filling; you're not actually losing the air.

Had a little trouble with back support on the front seat—next time I'll bring a rolled towel to support my lower back. It's good to bring a towel anyway so you can dry off the kayak before deflating and storing it. I suggest before taking the boat out you inflate it, test for leaks and do a test-sit to figure out how you want to arrange the seats and straps ahead of time; then use a sharpie to indicate who the seat is adjusted for, and where it needs to be stuck on the velcro.

Be gentle with the pump and paddles; some reviews mentioned they broke easily, though they seem sturdy enough to me—I don't think they'll stand up to much abuse, though.

Lots of fun for the price!

P.S: If you don't have PFDs, the ONYX MoveVent Dynamic Paddle Sports Life Vest (sold elsewhere on Amazon) works very well, and doesn't get in your way when paddling. Don't forget to buy a couple of paddle leashes with carabiners, too!
text_fidelity_b: Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump

Aegend Swim Goggles, 2 Pack Swimming Goggles No Leaking Adult Men Women Youth I’ve been pool swimming a few years now and I do wear glasses now since I’m over middle-aged.

I bought both the rounded goggles and flat lens goggles from these guys after reading an avid swimmers review speaking about only wearing flat lens. They’re the funky ones pro swimmers wear. Now I know why.

What a difference! I will never ever ever wear non-flatlands goggles again. I guarantee if you try each on, you will wonder why they even make curved lens goggles!

Goggles are made of a substance that does not lend itself to being curved. Every single thing is blurred. Above or below water. You put a flat lens pair on and boom! Every single thing is clear above and below water.

It’s such a pleasure. It’s like wiping grease away from a window and seeing clearly again. I thought I’d have issues with being near sighted… But of course water magnifies and with flat lenses, nothing was an issue.

All thanks to reading one of many reviews when trying to get to the bottom of what swim goggles on Amazon are great.

(In my pics the flat lens are the lighter lens ones reflecting my window better)

Me, I cannot stand up on this paddleboard as I have inner ear issues that cause me to have balance problems when things are...movable.  I can, however, sit and use the paddle to get around and with my legs dangling in the water, I have a fun day paddling around near the lake's shore, spending time outside in the sunshine on a pretty lake.  What could be better than that?  This SUP comes with everything you need, though I did get myself a small USB-powered air pump so I can pump this SUP up faster and my pump is about the size of a cell phone so the hand pump can be left behind, leaving a bit more space for the rest of the SUP's stuff.
